import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin"

/**
 * Server-side half of the dashboard plugin.
 *
 * The dashboard is a TUI-only feature; this entry exists so the package can be
 * loaded as an ordinary plugin while `./tui` supplies the terminal UI.
 */
export default Plugin.define({
  id: "session-dashboard",
  setup() {},
})

# opencode-session-dashboard [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@catronomix/opencode-session-dashboard)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@catronomix/opencode-session-dashboard) [![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/@catronomix/opencode-session-dashboard)](LICENSE) [![node](https://img.shields.io/node/v/@catronomix/opencode-session-dashboard)](https://nodejs.org) A fullscreen TUI overlay for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) that shows every open session and subagent in one overview. Ever feel like you are staring at the prompt box a bit too much, flicking through tabs to see what your agents are doing? Then this plugin is for you. See the session title, location, model, context fill, token hits and spenditure of each agent, including subagents — nesting supported. Maybe that's still TMI? No worries: the `f` key folds all subagents into single lines. Things can get boring after a few minutes of watching a swarm crawl through your precious token budget, so when idle you get treated to a groovy perlin noise animation. This plugin is entirely created and maintained with OpenCode, prompted with love. > **AI-generated.** This plugin was written almost entirely by an AI coding > agent (working under human direction and review). Treat it as such: read the > source before relying on it, and expect rough edges. Issues and pull requests > are welcome. --- ## Features - **Session cards** — one card per open tab: title, working directory, agent and model, a context-window bar, token totals, cost and age. The card whose tab is focused is marked `· focused`; running sessions get a green header dot and a yellow context bar (idle cards keep the green/amber/red usage ramp). - **Subagent tree** — child sessions are listed under their parent with a status and their current activity. Each subagent has an expandable detail block (path, agent · model, context bar, tokens, cost · age). - **Attention decorators** — a card or subagent that wants you swaps its status for the reason: `! permission` (yellow), `? question` (cyan), `× error` (red) or `◑ unread` (yellow). The card header rolls the strongest reason across the card and its subagents up to the column, and each subagent's header line gets the glyph before its title plus the reason leading its detail (`permission · 20% · 120k`). Strongest first: permission, question, error, unread. - **Keyboard selection** — move across cards with `←`/`→`, down into the tree with `↑`/`↓`, and open the selected session in the main TUI with `enter`. - **Close tabs in place** — `d` / `delete` closes the selected card's session tab without leaving the dashboard; the card list drops it and the rest stay put. Closing the last remaining tab closes it and leaves you on the new-session page, the same as closing the last tab outside the dashboard. - **Screensaver** — after two minutes of no input (configurable) the dashboard fades to a black background and the whole canvas is recoloured as an animation. Four looks ship in truecolor: **perlin drift** (the original groovy noise palette), **falling matrix** (green digital rain with a white-green head and a decaying trail), **sine sweep** (a soft band of drifting hue that travels down the screen) and **sparkling sky** (random grayscale characters fading gently in and out of the empty cells). `←`/`→` (or `↑`/`↓`) cycle the looks without waking the screensaver; any other key wakes it without leaking into the UI behind. - **Mouse** — hovering a column selects it (the highlight and `D`ynamic widths follow the pointer), clicking a session card opens it, clicking a subagent header row folds or unfolds it, clicking a subagent's detail block opens that subagent, and the wheel scrolls the view. - **`D`ynamic widths** — the selected card grows to 120% of the default width while every other card shrinks to 75%. - **Returns you where you were** — opening focuses the card for the tab you came from, and closing returns to that tab while it is still open (a new session when that tab was the last one) instead of dumping you on a new chat. - **Persisted preferences** — screensaver on/off and its current look, dynamic widths and the global fold state are stored across restarts via the plugin storage API. ## Keys | Key | Action | | --- | --- | | `ctrl+shift+d` / `alt+d` | Open the dashboard | | `esc` / `q` | Close (back to the previous tab) | | `←` / `→` | Previous / next session card (while the screensaver runs: previous / next look) | | `↑` / `↓` | Step from card into subagent rows and back (while the screensaver runs: previous / next look) | | `enter` / `return` | Open the selected session (card or subagent) and exit | | `d` / `delete` | Close the selected card's session tab (subagent rows close nothing; closing the last tab leaves for a new session) | | `space` | Expand/collapse the selection (one subagent row, or all rows of a selected card) | | `f` | Fold/expand all subagent details (persisted, clears per-row overrides) | | `shift+d` | `D`ynamic widths: emphasise the selected card, slim the others | | `a` | Show active sessions only | | `s` | Toggle the screensaver on/off (persisted; re-enabling shows it at once) | | `PgUp` / `PgDn` | Scroll a page | | `g` / `G` | Jump to top / bottom | ### Mouse | Action | Result | | --- | --- | | Hover a card | Select that column (highlight follows the pointer; the row resets to the card) | | Hover a subagent row | Select that row as well as its column | | Click a session card | Open that session (same as `enter` on the card) | | Click a subagent header row | Expand/collapse that subagent's detail block | | Click a subagent detail block | Open that subagent's session | | Wheel up / down | Scroll the view three rows per notch | Moving the pointer never wakes the screensaver (hovering is not activity); a click or a wheel notch does. ## Attention Nothing pops up over the dashboard: a session that needs you says so on its own header. Four moments are recognised, strongest first: | Decorator | Meaning | | --- | --- | | `! permission` | A tool is waiting for approval: the header turns yellow and reads `permission` | | `? question` | An open question/form is waiting: cyan, reads `question` | | `× error` | The host flagged the tab's last reply as failed: red, reads `error` | | `◑ unread` | An unread reply is waiting in the tab: yellow, reads `unread` | A subagent carries its own decorator on its tree line (`├─ ! builder` with `permission · 20% · 120k` as the detail), and the column's header shows the strongest reason found anywhere in that card's subagent family, so a blocked subagent is visible without folding anything open. Pending permissions and forms are synced once per session when the dashboard opens and then kept live by the host's events. ## Screensaver looks After the idle delay the dashboard goes black and the whole canvas is recoloured as an animation. Every look runs in truecolor (no 256-colour approximation) and recolours the glyphs that are already on screen, so nothing is re-laid out. While the screensaver is up, `←`/`↑` show the previous look and `→`/`↓` the next one; the arrows do not wake it, and the chosen look is remembered across restarts. Any other key wakes the dashboard. | # | Look | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | `perlin drift` | Smooth 3D Perlin noise through the spectrum palette, floored at a readable dark grey | | 2 | `falling matrix` | Green digital rain: one stream per column at its own speed, near-white head and a decaying trail | | 3 | `sine sweep` | Soft horizontal band of drifting hue travelling down the screen | | 4 | `sparkling sky` | Random narrow grayscale glyphs fading gently in and out of the empty cells | The current look, its number and its name are shown in the header clock while the screensaver runs. ## Settings Settings live in `~/.config/opencode/session-dashboard.json` (or `$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR/session-dashboard.json`). The file is written with the defaults on first run: ```json { "width": 45, "screensaverSeconds": 120 } ``` | Key | Default | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | `width` | `45` | Default card width in columns, clamped to 40–100 | | `screensaverSeconds` | `120` | Idle seconds before the screensaver starts, clamped to 10–3600 | Bad or missing values fall back to the defaults; a malformed file never breaks the dashboard. The persisted view toggles (`s`, `D`, `f`) and the current screensaver look are stored by the host, not in this file. ## Install ### From npm (recommended) ```sh opencode plugin add @catronomix/opencode-session-dashboard ``` or add it to the global `opencode.json(c)` yourself — a bare name resolves the current release, `@next` follows the prerelease channel: ```jsonc { "plugins": ["@catronomix/opencode-session-dashboard"] } ``` Then restart the TUI. The package ships its sources and resolves `@opencode/plugin`, `@opentui/*` and `solid-js` from OpenCode's own runtime, so the plugin needs no `node_modules` of its own. `opencode plugin check` reports newer releases and `opencode plugin update` installs them. If you want a frozen install, pin any published version you see in `npm view @catronomix/opencode-session-dashboard versions` — otherwise leave the name bare so updates keep flowing. ### From source (development) OpenCode loads plugins from `~/.config/opencode/plugins//`. The installed copy is **source-only**: OpenCode resolves `@opencode/plugin`, `@opentui/*` and `solid-js` from its own runtime, so the plugin directory needs no `node_modules` (and a local copy would shadow the host's instances). ```bash git clone https://github.com/catronomix/opencode-dashboard-plugin.git opencode-session-dashboard cd opencode-session-dashboard npm install # dev dependencies, for typecheck and tests only npm run deploy # copies src/*.ts|tsx to ~/.config/opencode/plugins/session-dashboard ``` Then restart the TUI. `npm run deploy` wipes and replaces the target directory, so local edits belong in `src/` here, never in the installed copy. Use either the path entry or the package entry, never both: two copies that resolve to the same plugin ID fight over the same hooks. ## Development ```bash npm test # node --test: dashboard rendering/layout/keys/screensavers + npm-readiness gate rules npm run typecheck # tsc --noEmit npm run release-check # pack + install the tarball the way a consumer does npm run deploy # copy the sources into the live plugin directory ``` The TUI half of a plugin has no console, so runtime diagnostics are appended to `%TEMP%/session-dashboard-debug.log` (`$TMPDIR` elsewhere). Nothing else is written to disk. ### Close-out A behaviour change is only live once it is deployed: run `npm run deploy` after the checks pass, then confirm the installed copy really has the new code instead of trusting the exit code alone. Compare hashes of `src/` against `~/.config/opencode/plugins/session-dashboard/` (e.g. `Get-FileHash` on Windows, `sha256sum` elsewhere); every file must match. A running OpenCode TUI keeps the plugin it loaded at startup, so restart it to pick the change up. `npm run deploy` is safe to repeat and never leaves stale files behind (it wipes the target first). ### Layout | File | Role | | --- | --- | | `src/index.ts` | Server-side plugin entry; the dashboard itself is TUI-only | | `src/tui.tsx` | Plugin setup, routing/close logic, view models, attention detection, selection and keymap | | `src/render.ts` | Pure canvas renderer: card layout/widths, cards, attention decorators, subagent detail blocks, chrome, rows, mouse hit-testing | | `src/config.ts` | Settings file path, parsing and clamping (width, screensaver delay) | | `src/view.ts` | View types (including the attention kinds), tree flattening and the token/cost/age formatters | | `src/palette.ts` | Screensaver looks (noise, matrix, sine sweep, sparkling sky) and their truecolor LUTs | | `scripts/deploy.mjs` | Copy `src/*.ts|tsx` into the local plugin directory | | `test/dashboard.test.ts` | Regression tests for layout, selection and screensaver | | `test/npm-readiness.test.mjs` | Rules for publishable metadata and version-agnostic README install text | | `scripts/release-check.mjs` | Consumer-side release gate (pack, install, metadata) | | `test/bench.ts` | Frame-timing harness for `buildRows`, run manually (`node test/bench.ts`) | Rendering is kept pure (`render.ts`) so it can be asserted on without a terminal; all animation and I/O live in `tui.tsx`. --- ## Notes - The plugin targets `@opencode/plugin` ≥ 2.1.4 and `@opentui/*` ≥ 0.6.6. - `npm run deploy` targets the default config directory (`~/.config/opencode/plugins`); edit the `target` path in `scripts/deploy.mjs` if yours differs. - This repository is not affiliated with the OpenCode project. ## License MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).
